report.source_text: Histopathological examination of the sections showed atrophic epidermis with mild hyperkeratosis and flattened rete ridges focally. The underlying papillary was showing a band-like mucin deposit along with focal sclerosis. The middle and deep dermis had patchy mucin along with focal fibrosis. Cuffing of mild to moderate lymphomononuclear infiltrate was observed around perivascular areas in the dermis. Few of the blood vessels were showing endothelial cell proliferation (Figure 2a-c). Scant subcutaneous tissue was available in the biopsy. The result of Alcian blue staining for dermal mucin was positive (Fig. 2d).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old Hindu woman presented with a 1.5-year history of painful depigmented lesions characterized by porcelain-white atrophic papules with surrounding erythema distributed over the trunk, upper limbs, thighs, and chest. Associated systemic symptoms included 7-8 years of joint pain and recent 3-month history of headache, giddiness, and ocular pain. Physical examination confirmed porcelain-white atrophic papules with surrounding erythema and mild tenderness. Histopathology of skin biopsy demonstrated characteristic features of Degos disease: atrophic epidermis with hyperkeratosis and flattened rete ridges, band-like mucin deposit with focal sclerosis in the papillary dermis, patchy mucin and focal fibrosis in the middle and deep dermis, perivascular lymphomononuclear infiltrate, endothelial cell proliferation in blood vessels, and positive Alcian blue staining for dermal mucin. Systemic investigations to assess for systemic complications included abdominal ultrasound (unremarkable), ophthalmologic examination (myopic astigmatism, unrelated to ocular pain), and stool occult blood test (negative). Owing to the absence of systemic complications, the patient was diagnosed with benign cutaneous Degos disease. Treatment with antiplatelet agents (aspirin 75 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg once daily) resulted in cessation of new lesion formation within 1 month.
